title: Basics of Scientific Rigor and Reproducibility
audience: Clinical learners practicing transparent outlier handling in EHR-style data
objectives: Explore simulated hospital admission and outcome data for CHF readmission analysis.
Visualize and detect outliers in age, length of stay, BNP, and sodium.
Calculate 1.5x IQR thresholds and inspect flagged patient rows.
Compare summary statistics before and after outlier exclusion.
Evaluate remove, winsorize, and median-imputation strategies in clinical context.

sections.name: Clinical Dataset Overview
sections.how_to_use: Review each variable and remember that extreme clinical values may be valid, errors, or clinically important signals.

sections.name: Visualize Outliers with Boxplots
sections.how_to_use: Select a variable, inspect the box plot, and note patient IDs and values that look unusual.

sections.name: Calculate Outlier Thresholds
sections.purpose: Apply the 1.5x IQR rule to clinical variables.
sections.how_to_use: Choose a variable and review Q1, Q3, IQR, bounds, and flagged patient rows.

sections.name: Effect on Clinical Summary Statistics
sections.purpose: Show how outliers influence clinical summaries.
sections.how_to_use: Compare mean, standard deviation, and median with all values versus no outliers.

sections.name: Outlier Handling Approaches
sections.how_to_use: Choose a strategy and explain clinical risks if valid extreme values are mishandled.

sections.name: Reflection
sections.purpose: Connect outlier handling to reproducible clinical research.
sections.how_to_use: Write what should be reported in methods and how poor handling could affect clinical conclusions.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through dataset review, boxplot inspection, IQR thresholds, statistics comparison, handling strategy, and reflection.
For clinical users, emphasize that outliers can be data errors, rare but valid clinical states, or important safety signals.
Help learners avoid automatically deleting clinically extreme values.
